items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: And who else was in the band? Oh, a trombone player named Atkins.

ctx.x: Oh, boy. Let's see, he had Sax Mallard, out of Denver, Colorado, alto player; a boy named Johnson, we called him Head, 'cause he had a [poll wrinkled] head. He had one of them saddle heads. So we called him Head Johnson. Trumpet player. And who else? Oh, a boy played tenor saxophone. That played with dentures, and they were always loose. We called him Gummy. But his name was Wright. I can't remember

his first name. He would do most of the arranging for the band. And who else was in the band? Oh, a trombone player named Atkins. Played good trombone. I can't think of his first name, either. But he finally wound up working up working with Earl Hines. And John Ewing, at the same time. And another trombone player that committed suicide, shot himself in the head. I think he was drunk, playing Russian Roulette. Roulette, roulette. All right.
Well, with this band, we were supposed to be making 18 dollars a week.
